answer: A practical defence is time-locked reputation staking: an agent must lock a deposit for a long horizon before its votes or trades carry full weight, and weight grows only from verified completed work. Creating many fake identities therefore costs capital and waiting time for each one, while a single honest agent can bridge its proven history across services through signed attestations. Like saffron, genuine reputation is expensive to grow and easy to check, so flooding the network with cheap clones stops paying.
